scope: Course authored from the programme training deck; deck model cross-checked against recruitment literature Nov 2026

sources.supporting_text: ClairLabs - AI-Enabled Digital Solution for Patient Recruitment: participant identification, qualification and warm handover across the journey; AI-driven funnel; HCP, data-driven and advocacy outreach; site alignment and go-live; patient-centric architecture; go-live roadmap; differentiators and case studies. Deck case figures (61% more patients, 70-90% non-conversion) are vendor-reported and cited as deck figures in training, not independent findings.
sources.title: ClairLabs Patient Recruitment Deck

sources.locator: JMIR 2020 systematic review and meta-analysis; Cambridge JCTS meta-analysis
sources.supporting_text: Online recruitment is effective vs traditional methods; social media about twice as cost-effective as non-social methods, with high variability between studies. Supports the deck's multichannel/programmatic funnel and retargeting logic.
sources.title: Online recruitment effectiveness literature

sources.locator: SMA advocacy case (60% timeline improvement); PRISM rare-disease DTC study (40.1% lead generation); GO2 lung cancer advocacy-led site network
sources.supporting_text: Advocacy-group partnerships materially improve recruitment timelines and lead generation, especially in rare disease; registries connect pre-identified, opted-in patients. Supports the deck's PAG-and-registry model.
sources.title: Patient advocacy and registry evidence

sources.locator: Tufts CSDD via TrialNotice 2026: 11% zero-enroll, 37% under-enroll, 36.3% screen failure, 19.1% dropout; ACRP 2025: median activation 140-167 days vs 90-120 target
sources.supporting_text: Recruitment is the rate-limiting step; most sites under-enroll and activation is slow. Supports the deck's rapid-activation, hyper-localized, live-analytics site model and the screen-failure reduction claim directionally.
sources.title: Site activation and enrollment benchmarks
